# kde-vnc-cdp — the KDE desktop over VNC, with the full CDP surface

## The stack

`pod-kde-vnc`'s desktop, unchanged, plus the browser automation every other streaming pod has:

| layer | provided by | detail |
|---|---|---|
| base image | `podcdi.pod-cdi` | CachyOS; the GPU driver is injected from the host through CDI |
| desktop | `pod-kde-vnc` → `kde-vnc-session` | headless sway → wayvnc `:5900`; nested KWin + plasmashell on `wayland-kde`; the ambient session env |
| browser | `pod-chrome-cdp` → `chrome-cdp` | `chrome-wrapper` (CDP on 127.0.0.1:9223, Windows UA, `chrome-windows` extension), `cdp-proxy` (0.0.0.0:**9222**), `browser-open` (`$BROWSER`), `chrome-restart`, `BROWSER_CDP_URL` |
| MCP | `pod-chrome-devtools-mcp` (composed by chrome-cdp) | `chrome-devtools-mcp` over Streamable HTTP on **9224** |
| this repo | `kde-vnc-cdp-session` | declares Chrome as a SUPERVISED program on the Plasma socket |

Ports are inherited from the candies: **5900** (VNC), **9222** (CDP), **9224** (MCP). The image
declares none of its own.

## Why Chrome is a PLASMA window and supervised

- **On `wayland-kde`, not `wayland-0`.** sway's `wayland-0` is the compositor BEHIND the fullscreen
  KWin window: a browser there is invisible in the stream. Chrome must join KWin's socket so it is
  a Plasma window the VNC user sees and can take over.
- **Supervised.** The `chrome` service execs `chrome-wrapper` with `wait_for: /tmp/wayland-kde`, so
  KWin binds its socket before the browser starts, a slow session fails the SERVICE with a reason,
  and an exit restarts the browser (`start_sec: 5` resets the retry budget past the startup
  transient). A compositor-driven launch cannot do any of that, and a hand launch would put a
  SECOND browser on the same `--user-data-dir`.
- **Maximized by the wrapper** (`--start-maximized`), asserted on BOTH sides: the browser's own
  `window.outerWidth/outerHeight` against `screen.avail*` (`MAXOK`), and the compositor's window
  geometry via `kdotool`. The flag alone proves nothing on Wayland — `xdg-shell.set_maximized` is
  a request, and KWin's placement runs after it.

## What works, and what does not

- **Every `cdp:` method** against the browser EXCEPT `screenshot`: `status`, `list`, `open`,
  `close`, `url`, `text`, `html`, `eval`, `axtree`, `wait`, `coords`, `raw`, `click`, `type`. Use
  `context: [runtime]` in a bed; `deploy` is not a check mode and a `deploy`-scoped check step
  is skipped.
- **`cdp: screenshot` is a measured GPU-Wayland limit here** (`opencharly/plugin-cdp#14`): the
  surface capture never returns and the plugin's renderer-view fallback comes back uniformly white
  on every attempt (4/4, 99 s). It is not asserted — a poll cannot fix a capture that is blank by
  construction — and the visual claim belongs to the VNC frame (`vnc: screenshot` + host OCR),
  which is what the streamed user actually sees.
- **`cdp: spa-*` does NOT apply.** Those methods drive a Selkies SPA page (canvas + overlay input);
  this pod streams VNC. For desktop-level pointer work use `cdp: coords` for the LOCATE half and
  `vnc: click` / `vnc: type` for the DELIVER half.
- **`wl:` is window management only on KWin.** `plugin-wl` routes KWin's
  toplevel/focus/close/fullscreen/minimize/geometry through `kdotool` and fail-fasts the wlroots
  paths: no pointer, no keyboard, no clipboard, no resolution. Pointer and keyboard input in this
  pod come from `vnc:`.
- **`cdp: coords`' `Sway:` line names the nested KWin window, not Chrome** — the point is over
  the compositor's window, which is what the sway tree can see. The `Desktop:` line is the one to
  hand to `vnc: click`; the `Viewport:` line is browser-relative.
- **The ambient session env is the image's DEFAULT, not a guarantee.** `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-kde`
  and `KDE_SESSION_VERSION=6` come from the composed desktop candy, so anything started inside
  lands in Plasma by default. A CHECK STEP must still name its display: the runner forwards the
  operator's environment into the container (measured), and the supervised `chrome` service states
  its own `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` for the same reason.

## Testing (`check-kde-vnc-cdp-pod`)

Needs a host with a GPU exposed through CDI (the CPU-only sibling to run instead is
`check-sway-browser-vnc-pod`, which covers the helpers' unsupervised branch).

| what | verb |
|---|---|
| six services RUNNING, Chrome stable ≥25s | `command:` `supervisorctl status` |
| KWin fullscreen; hardware OpenGL | `command:` `swaymsg -t get_tree`, KWin `supportInformation` |
| Chrome is a KWin client, maximized (both sides) | `command:` `kdotool search/getwindowgeometry`, `cdp: eval` `MAXOK` |
| every `cdp:` method | `cdp:` steps (status…close) |
| the VNC frame SHOWS the page | `vnc: screenshot` (captures the desktop) + a HOST-side `command:` running `tesseract` over that PNG — the `vnc:` verb does not carry `artifact_contains_text` (measured) |
| VNC DRIVES the page | `vnc: click` at the maximized window's centre + `vnc: type` into a CDP-focused field, read back by `cdp: eval` |
| `$BROWSER`, `chrome-restart` | `command:` `browser-open …`, `chrome-restart`, then `cdp: status` |
| the MCP catalog | `mcp: ping`, `mcp: list-tools` |

The VNC frame is read by `tesseract` ON THE HOST (not in the image), driven from a host-side
`command:` step because `vnc:` has no `artifact_contains_text`. The marker the frame carries is a
SINGLE WORD (`CHARLYCDP`): a hyphenated token is the one thing OCR reliably mangles. Prove the
assertion can fail (a word that is not on screen must go RED) before trusting a green one.

## The pod-to-pod cross-deployment CDP probe (`check-cross-kde-cdp-pod`)

This repo also carries the org's ONLY witness of pod→pod CDP rendering, rebuilt on CachyOS+KDE
after its Fedora predecessor was retired (opencharly/distro-fedora#138, #140):

- **The web SUBJECT is the bed root** — the `kde-web-subject` image, a plain CachyOS base
  (`cachyos.cachyos`, NOT the GPU pod base) composing `pod-web-layer`'s fixture: nginx serving
  `charly-fixture-web-content-marker` on 8080.
- **The KDE pod is a SIBLING DRIVER member** (`desktop:` under the bed). Its `cdp:` steps run on
  that member's venue and navigate to `http://${HOST:check-cross-kde-cdp-pod}:8080` — the SUBJECT's
  container name on the shared `charly` net, not a host port, so no Chrome is baked into the
  subject and nothing goes through the host loopback.
- A `vnc: screenshot` + OCR step then proves the cross-pod page is what the streamed user SEES.

Needs a GPU host for the DRIVER member only. `pod-web-layer` needed a `distro.arch` section
for the fixture to compose on CachyOS at all.
